title: Science Card
$comment: CANONICAL DEFINITION. This file is the single source of truth for the Science Card abstraction across the Squad / Loom / Lean Genius effort (rjwalters/squad#20, rjwalters/loom#6109, rjwalters/lean-genius#43705). Other repositories are expected to vendor this file verbatim — keeping its $id and version, and adding a provenance comment pointing back here — or reference it by $id, rather than authoring their own copy. If you need a field this schema does not have, change it HERE and bump `version`, so divergence is detectable by comparing $id + version. Runtime-neutral by construction: no Claude-, Codex-, or Squad-specific fields.
description: A durable, runtime-neutral record of one research question as it moves through the falsification-driven phase cycle QUESTION -> DIVERGE -> ORIENT -> HYPOTHESIZE -> DERIVE -> ATTACK -> SIMULATE -> EXPERIMENT -> REPLICATE -> SUPPORTED | FALSIFIED | INCONCLUSIVE, with LEARN -> PIVOT loops. Negative outcomes (FALSIFIED, INCONCLUSIVE, ABANDONED) are first-class results, not deletions.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the card was written against. Matches the schema document's top-level `version`.

id.description: Stable identifier for the card, unique within its store. Squad uses the room-local integer row id; other runtimes may use strings or UUIDs.

title.description: Short human-readable name for the card.

question.description: The research question the card exists to answer.

phase.description: Current position in the phase cycle.

status.description: Claim-level status. OPEN until the card reaches a terminal phase. Deliberately distinct from any individual evidence item's own status: a `verified` derivation does NOT make an empirical claim SUPPORTED.

claim_kind.description: What kind of claim the card makes. `empirical` and `mixed` claims require empirical evidence (experiment or observation) before they can be SUPPORTED; a `formal` claim can be SUPPORTED on derivation/formal-check evidence alone.

origin_method.description: How the idea was generated (e.g. 'divergence round 3', 'literature gap', 'anomaly in run 12').

contributors.description: Identities that contributed to the card. Runtime-neutral: any string identity, not tied to a particular agent vendor.

changed_assumptions.description: Standard assumptions this card deliberately drops or alters.

proposed_mechanism.description: The mechanism proposed to explain the phenomenon.

model_statement.description: The mathematical or model-level statement of the claim.

discriminating_prediction.description: The prediction that distinguishes this card's claim from the null.

decisive_falsifier.description: The observation that would decisively falsify the claim.

cheapest_test.description: The cheapest test that could produce the decisive falsifier.

prior_art_status.description: How the claim stands relative to known prior art.

confidence.description: Self-assessed confidence in the claim, 0 (none) to 1 (certain). Never a substitute for evidence.

evidence.description: Typed evidence items, each with its own provenance and its own evidence-level status.

attempts.description: Things tried, whether or not they worked.

attacks.description: Deliberate attempts to break the claim.

insights.description: Findings worth keeping regardless of the card's outcome.

post_mortems.description: What was learned after a terminal outcome, especially a negative one.

transitions.description: Append-only phase history, oldest first. The first entry has a null from_phase (card genesis).

updated_ts.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last mutation.

evidence_status.description: Status of THIS evidence item only. `verified` means the item itself checks out (a proof compiles, a run reproduces) — it never means the card's claim is scientifically true.

provenance.description: Where the evidence came from: a file path, commit, DOI, run id, instrument. Required and non-empty — evidence without provenance is an assertion.
